blocks.heading: A business plan
blocks.text: A business plan is a document containing the business objectives and important details about the operations and finance of the firm. It explains what the enterprise intends to do, for whom, how it will operate and how it expects to finance the activity. It supports coordinated decisions, communication with potential funders and later review. Forecasts are assumptions to test, not promises that sales or funding will occur. A useful plan connects its sections: planned demand must fit capacity, staffing, spending and cash timing. A polished document cannot compensate for unrealistic evidence. Review the plan when conditions change rather than treating completion of the document as completion of the business.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Nela Meals proposes a small weekday lunch service for nearby workers. Its plan should connect customer evidence with meals, collection arrangements, staff, equipment and finance. A menu alone does not explain whether the proposed service can operate and pay its bills.
